description: Ticket texts an agent might write, labeled with whether they assert an outage. The verifier's ticket_outage_claim_unsupported check and the ticket grounding guardrail both read these through one matcher, so both must agree on every case. `claims` is what the text means. `matcher` is what the shared matcher returns today, and differs from `claims` only on shapes documented as wrong in the verifier's module docstring.

cases.text: Customer was hit by the January outage.
Customer reports downtime right after signup.
Service disruption during the first week, customer requests credit.
Two incidents affected the account last month.
Your service was down for three days after purchase.

Refund request
Customer was affected by the outages in January.
Order shows no outage on record. Customer hit by the January outage.
Order shows no outage on record; customer was hit by the January outage.
No outage was involved in this purchase.
Couldn't find any outage for this customer in the logs.
We cannot confirm an outage on this account.
I can't see any downtime in the window in question.
Nothing in the order record supports an outage.
None of the incidents affected this order.
Customer asked about billing only.
Declined refund, purchase is past the window.
this was incidental to the main request
Engineering could not reproduce the outage.
Was there an outage around the time I signed up?
cases.known_wrong: a question reads as an assertion

cases.text: I'd like to report an incident with my delivery.
cases.known_wrong: incident is a generic support word

cases.text: There was no warning before the outage hit my account.
cases.known_wrong: a negation inside the window that is about something else suppresses the claim

cases.text: An outage never happened on this account.
cases.known_wrong: a negation after the claim word is never seen
